author: Maya Yang
description:
More than 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River in mission being hailed as ‘Mississippi miracle’

Mariners and first responders who took part in the so-called “Mississippi miracle” rescue mission, which saw about 100 people pulled from the water after a tanker collided with a cruise ship, have said they are thankful “everything came out all right”.

The collision on Friday between the Atlantic Asphalt tanker and the American Heritage riverboat saw more than 30 people injured.

Continue reading...
title: First responders describe rescue efforts after New Orleans boat crash: ‘We have to save each other’

author: Associated Press
description:
Appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of Netanyahu’s outgoing government

The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

The new speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu. Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious policies following Kahana’s election.

Continue reading...
title: Israeli parliament elects new Knesset speaker backed by Netanyahu’s opponents

author: Anna Betts and Blake Montgomery
description:
Google’s Gmail also affected after problems reported in technological infrastructure in the US and worldwide

Thousands reported disruptions to Google’s Gmail and Apple’s iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday, according to Downdetector. Apple confirmed the outages in a statement but said it had resolved them; Google said it had not seen internal signs of outages.

Apple’s own system status page as of 2.30pmET shows problems with services such as the App Store, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps and AppleCare.

Continue reading...
title: Apple outage: iPhone apps suffer disruption days after major Microsoft issues

author: Press Association
description:
• Teenager says ‘thank you for everything’ in video

  • Gabriel expected to join Real Madrid

JJ Gabriel appears to have confirmed his departure from Manchester United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media.

The teenager, who has not played a competitive game for the first team, joined as a 10-year-old in 2020 but has been absent from the club since he requested his registration was cancelled in September before he turned 16 on 6 October.

Continue reading...
title: JJ Gabriel confirms Manchester United exit: ‘You gave me moments I will always treasure’

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
NSA issues ‘code yellow’ as NSANet, used by staff to share classified material, including top-secret intelligence, fails

The National Security Agency said on Tuesday that it had experienced “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after reports that its classified internal communications network had gone down.

In a statement, the agency said some internal systems were affected but that “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational” and its ability to defend national security continues. It said its infrastructure is built with “multiple layers of redundancy” to keep operations running during planned maintenance or unexpected events.

Continue reading...
title: National Security Agency network for internal communications goes down

author: Scott Murray
description:
• Nations League updates from the 7.45pm GMT kick-off

  • Live scores | Today’s Football Daily | And email Scott

Wales make six changes to their starting line-up following the 3-1 defeat in Norway. Two are enforced: Ethan Ampadu is suspended while Neco Williams is injured. In come Danny Ward, David Brooks, Connor Roberts, Rubin Colwill, Sorba Thomas and Josh Sheehan. Karl Darlow, Liam Cullen, Lewis Koumas and Brennan Johnson drop to the bench.

Wales: Ward, Roberts, Rodon, B Davies, Dasilva, Wilson, Sheehan, Brooks, D James, R Colwill, Thomas.

Continue reading...
title: Wales v Portugal: Nations League football – live

author: Daniel Harris
description:
ATP Finals updates, with play from 7.30pm GMT
Sign up for the Recap newsletter | Email Daniel

“Achieving the world No 1 status is something every player dreams of, but I feel like I’m the only world No 1 in tennis history that has to explain why it’s OK for me to be world No 1. Which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am”.

So said Alexander Zverev after becoming the first world No 1 to lose in straight sets immediately after establishing that status. He does, though, know why it’s like this. First of all, not everyone agrees with his assertion that “the accusations” against him of domestic violence “have been proven false”, so not everyone is happy with his new status. But there are sporting reasons too: the man unable to win majors when Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alc
title: Alexander Zverev v Ben Shelton: ATP Finals tennis group stage – live

author: Guy de Launey in Belgrade
description:
Celebrating supporters say they feel vindicated by arrival of Student List candidates in National Assembly

The paved plateau in front of Serbia’s National Assembly became an impromptu dancefloor, as mixed age groups joyfully whirled in a kolo. Drivers passing by sounded their horns, while hundreds of people waved flags, blew whistles and cheered. Every now and again, the crowd parted, allowing smartly dressed men and women to walk up the steps and into the building.

These were the candidates from the Student List, on their way to being sworn in as members of parliament, following their stunning victory in last month’s parliamentary elections. Those who had come to cheer them on displayed their feelings on badges, flags and placards.
title: Joy, hope and anger as Serbia student movement’s political novices enter parliament

author: Maya Yang
description:
A report analyzing more than 35,000 scripts finds that storylines address its causes, but individual actions remain more prominent than systemic solutions

Climate change and its causes are appearing more frequently in film and television, but entertainment continues to focus more on the consequences of the crisis and individual actions than large-scale solutions, according to a new report.

Released Tuesday and just weeks after Digger, the latest high-profile climate movie that features Tom Cruise as an oil tycoon, the report from the USC Annenberg School for Communications and Journalism and Good Energy, a nonprofit story consultancy, examines climate change in
title: Climate crisis more visible in film and TV but solutions remain rare, study finds

author: Ewan Murray in St Gallen
description:
The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job

The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.

There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching in to the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the
title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable

author: Sam Levin
description:
Thirty district attorneys challenged governor’s mass clemency, on behalf of victims’ families and advocates

California prosecutors and victims’ advocates have sued the state’s governor, Gavin Newsom, to stop him from commuting the death sentences of all 548 people facing execution in the state.

The district attorneys from 30 of California’s 58 counties filed the lawsuit on Monday, challenging the Democratic governor’s mass clemency action announced earlier this month, which would be the largest clearing of any death row in modern US histo
title: California DAs sue Gavin Newsom to stop death sentence commutations

author: Guardian staff
description:
Late-night hosts discussed the administration’s unhelpful response to the FAA’s rare ground stop this weekend

Late-night hosts responded to the FAA’s sudden, rare ground stop as Donald Trump shirks any responsibility for the transportation crisis.

Continue reading...
title: Jon Stewart on Trump administration response to air travel crisis: ‘So chaotic and amateurish’

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Infectious disease is now continually spreading after being eliminated for 26 years, with more than 5,400 US cases

The US lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities announced, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the US after being eliminated for 26 years.

The announcement comes as the US endures the worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases and eight deaths in 2026.

Continue reading...
title: US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
US officials ‘continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute’ plot to detonate a ‘dirty bomb’, report says

Donald Trump has claimed the US is “looking into” whether Iran is developing plans to detonate a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington, even as the White House said there are “no credible threats” at this time.

Trump said his administration takes the idea “very seriously”

Continue reading...
title: Trump claims US is ‘looking into’ Iranian bomb plot in Washington despite ‘no credible threats’

author: Guardian community team
description:
Do you have something you’d like to ask the man who’s been Sherlock’s right-hand man, a beloved hobbit and the voice of Gromit? Now is your chance

When he first charmed audiences in 2001 as phenomenally relatable everyman Tim in a lo-fi BBC mockumentary about office workers, he did so as a hugely loved supporting character. It wasn’t a given that he’d go on to be one of Britain’s most beloved actors, with a role in the highest grossing movie franchise ever, multiple Emmy wins and end up outshining everyone else who shared the screen with him.

Yet, in the decades since, that’s just what’s happened: Martin Freeman has starred in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, won one of his two Baftas for being the Dr Watson to Benedict Cumberbatch’s Sherlock Holmes and somehow become a cornerstone of Christmas, with roles in Richard Curtis’s Love Actually and Nativity.

Continue reading
title: Send us your questions for Martin Freeman

author: Sam Levine
description:
The stoppage was seemingly caused by the transition from copper telecommunication lines

As Republicans scramble to shift blame for the recent chaotic FAA flight stoppage, JD Vance took a new tact, claiming a Democratic focus on transgender sports issues were to blame.

During an interview on Fox News on Monday, host Laura Ingraham pressed Vance on why his fellow Republicans had not been able to fix issues with air traffic control even though they had controlled the White House and Congress for the last two years.

Continue reading...
title: JD Vance blames Democrats for flight stoppage, claiming ‘obsession with men in women’s sports’

author: Stuart Heritage
description:
If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market

Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt. The month before, Brad Pitt bought a mansion from one of the Killers. In 2022, Adele bought Sylvester Stallone’s old house, but only if he let her keep his Rocky statue. Aaron Paul recently sold a house that he bought from The Big Bang Theory’s Jim Parsons, who bought it from Robert Pattinson, after it was previously owned by Noah Wyle, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Tim Curry and the guy who directed Legally Blonde.

If this makes it sound to you as if there are only a handful of celebrity-friendly homes on earth, and celebrities spend their lives swapping them around among themselves, then you’re right.

Continue
title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes

author: Wendy Syfret
description:
Claudia O’Doherty plays a chipper content creator dissociating through the apocalypse, in a 2019 web series that’s more relevant than ever

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

For most of her career, Australian actor and comedian Claudia O’Doherty has played on her adorable persona in the whimsical worlds of Bluey, Our Flag Means Death and Love, among others. She’s all big eyes and bangs, stealing scenes and hearts.

But, as anyone who saw surprise hit Maddie’s Secret would know, O’Doherty is supremely satisfying as a villain. In John Early’s surreal yet oddly moving tale of a female food influencer’s battle with an eating disorder, O’Doherty broke bad as Maddie’s nemesis, Emily.
title: Sarah’s Channel: a beauty blogger ignores the end of the world in this increasingly relatable spoof

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise

Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne Collins. This one has another of the series’ convoluted faux-mythic subtitles: Sunrise on the Reaping. What, “harvest dawn” not old-timey enough?

Well, “reaping” in fact refers to an annual process by which ordinary smudgy faced, raggedy clothed people are chosen at random for compulsory participation in this futurist dystopia’s brutal, televised survival contest to the death: a bread-and-circuses nightmare with which the rulers keep the populace in a cowed and pacified state. In this Darwinian process, competitors strategically team up with (and then betray) some players against others in the short term, to stay in the game.
title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review – surreally awful prequel to the Katniss Everdeen era

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
Former 007 George Lazenby was supportive while The Lighthouse director Robert Eggers reveals what Pattinson was doing when the news broke

• Robert Pattinson is James Bond. What happens next?
• Peter Bradshaw’s take
• Pattinson’s journey to James Bond
• Behind Bond’s bankability

Film industry figures including Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and former Bond actor George Lazenby have reacted to the news that Robert Pattinson has been
title: ‘Sorry, I’m still in love with Daniel Craig’: Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and more react to Robert Pattinson as James Bond

author: Eric Berger
description:
Inflation and expanding services are drawing more people to public libraries, offering everything from books to job support and free activities

Public libraries have experienced a surge in demand in the last few years, a welcome development in the US amid concerns about federal funding cuts and a decline in literacy rates.

For example, public libraries in Union county, North Carolina received 433,517 visitors during fiscal year 2026, a 20% increase from just two years earlier, according to a county report.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Come stay all day’: US libraries see rise in visitors as patrons seek affordable resources

author: Annie Nichol and Jess Nichol
description:
After so many years of hearing our family’s tragedy invoked in support of capital punishment, we wanted to make clear where we actually stand

For more than three decades, our sister Polly Klaas’s murder has been used to justify California’s death penalty.

When people debate the merit of punitive policies passed in Polly’s name, politicians, advocates, even strangers have asked: “What about Polly?” As if our loss were an argument that speaks for itself.

Continue reading...
title: Polly Klaas’s murder is routinely used to justify the death penalty. As her sisters, we oppose it | Annie Nichol and Jess Nichol

author: Associated Press
description:
• Player in ‘category one’ status after US Open win

  • Golfer ineligible for PGA Tour due to blanket ban

Bryson DeChambeau will play on the DP World Tour for the 2027 season following the hughly publicised demise of LIV Golf.

DeChambeau is ineligible to join the PGA Tour, where he has not played for more than four years, due to a blanket ban on LIV players that runs for 12 months from the date of their last tournament appearance on the Saudi Arabia-funded circuit.

Continue reading...
title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour for 2027 after demise of LIV Golf

author: Mos Hannan, Usayd Younis, Hannah Bush Bailey, Ekaterina Ochagavia and Lindsay Poulton
description:
It is 40 years since a racially charged attack at a curry house led to Satpal Ram’s conviction for murder, but today Britain’s post-pub curry culture still has a dark side. Ram spent 24 years in prison before a global campaign for justice, led by bands including Asian Dub Foundation and Primal Scream, secured his release from prison. His case raises crucial questions about the UK’s ongoing struggle for racial equality

Continue reading...
title: After Eight: the story of Satpal Ram - documentary

author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
description:
Leaders of India and Japan join for talks on military exercises, AI and rare earths as a counter to Chinese power

Donald Trump and Anthony Albanese have heralded plans for new joint Quad military exercises designed to push back on China’s expansionist ambitions, promising the grouping with India and Japan will guarantee “peace through strength.”

Albanese met Trump, India’s Nahrendra Modi and Japan’s Sanae Takaichi in Manila late on Tuesday in talks about enhanced cooperation on AI, critical minerals, infrastructure and maritime security.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Peace through strength’: Albanese and Trump hail progress on Quad alliance

author: Janine van Wyk
description:
In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations

I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.

As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.
title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’

author: Associated Press
description:
• Springboks’ head coach makes contentious remarks

  • South Africa due to face Ireland next in Dublin

South Africa’s head coach Rassie Erasmus has questioned whether the failure of match officials to spot what he perceived to be illegal tackles by opponents could amount to “match-fixing” or “manipulation of the game or result”.

Erasmus’s contentious remarks were made ahead of the Springboks’ upcoming Test match against Ireland at a press conference on Monday. He has previously been banned by World Rugby on two separate occasions for hostile comments toward match officials.

Continue reading...
title: Rassie Erasmus launches ‘match-fixing’ diatribe over officials after defeat

author: Kiran Stacey and Richard Partington
description:
Author of long-awaited report says money saved in benefit cuts will mostly be used to fund new job support system

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?

Alan Milburn has said his plan to get more young people into work will save the government only £200m a year as the cost of job support swallows up almost all of the anticipated cuts to benefits.

The former health secretary unveiled his long-awaited report into youth unemployment on Tuesday morning, urging ministers to cut disability and sickness payments for under-25s and invest the money in back-to-work schemes. Figures contained in the report show that his plan
title: Alan Milburn says his plan to get young people into work will save only £200m a year

author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
description:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy

In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.

Continue reading...
title: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit

author: Becca Andrews
description:
Charismatic worship, which promises ‘deliverance’ from evil, has taken hold across Christian churches, the right and on social media

Slumped on the ground, the young woman pressed her forehead against the warm pavement of a twilit parking lot in Columbia, Tennessee.

Two other women dressed in white T-shirts identifying them as members of the ministry attended to her, praying over her prone body, speaking to her in low, urgent tones. Her whimpers escalated into moans and then crescendoed into guttural cries: “No! No! No!”

Continue reading...
title: ‘I know I sound crazy’: the creep of demons into American evangelical churches

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Long-awaited report on Neets will be published this morning as author acknowledges that there will be initial costs

Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people

The UK unemployment rate has unexpectedly fallen as the government prepares to release the Alan Milburn report on the youth jobs crisis, Phillip Inman reports.

Good morning. Few government reports have been as long-awaited and well-trailed as the Alan Milburn report into youth unemployment, or Neets (young people not in education, employment or training), that is finally being published this morning. The title, From a Welfare State to a Working State, gives a clue as to the extent of Milburn’s ambition and, if it gets i
title: Youth unemployment plan could cut welfare bill before election, says Milburn, but overall savings will take years – UK politics live

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• Deal will run to 2031 and worth about £300,000 a week

  • Jurriën Timber also agrees fresh contract extension

Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year contract at Arsenal, with the England midfielder poised to match Bukayo Saka’s status as the highest-paid player at the Premier League champions.

Representatives for Rice, who won his 82nd cap in England’s thrilling win over Spain on Sunday, have been in talks for months about extending the deal he signed in 2023 after a record £105m move from West Ham. That is believed to be worth about £250,000 a week and is due to expire in 2028, although Arsenal have the option of a further 12 months.

Continue reading...
title: Declan Rice agrees new Arsenal contract making him club’s joint highest-paid player

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Owner of JPS cigarettes, Golden Virginia tobacco, Blu vapes and Rizla has launched huge cost-cutting drive

  • Business live – latest updates

Imperial Brands, the owner of Davidoff cigarettes and Blu vapes, is slashing up to 4,600 jobs in a huge cost-cutting drive, as it uses more AI and other technologies.

The Bristol-based company said this year 2,100 roles would go globally, and it plans a further reduction of between 2,100 and 2,500 jobs by the end of 2030.

Continue reading...
title: Tobacco group Imperial Brands to axe up to 4,600 jobs as it uses more AI

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Agreement secured by Equity union gives actors rights over payment and consent when digital replicas are used

Actors in the UK are to be given more rights over their “digital replicas” as part of a new agreement on AI protections with TV and film producers, secured after a growing on-set backlash.

Under a wide-ranging new deal secured by Equity, the actors’ union, performers will have the rights to be paid when their digital replicas are used and to consent to whether their digital replica is used or not.

Continue reading...
title: Actors in UK to get more rights over their ‘digital replicas’ in deal on AI protections

author: Rahul Bhattacharya
description:
The Italian who became kingmaker in the world’s largest democracy charts her remarkable journey

By any measure, it is one of the most extraordinary political stories of our age: a shy Italian girl locks eyes with the scion of an Indian political family, falls instantly and steadfastly in love, “transplanting herself” as a result, suffers soul-shattering tragedies, then takes the reins of power in the world’s largest democracy. It is a life that spans the extremes of privilege and distress, and half a century of seismic national history.

No wonder publishers have been keen to secure the memoirs of the famously guarded Sonia Gandhi, soon to turn 80. Yet when the chance came, the deal with the country’s biggest publisher, Penguin Random House India, fell through at the last minute over what it termed “an impasse over a particular issue” in the text, with HarperCollins stepping into the breach. For those unfamiliar with the sensitive political context, the Nehru-Gandhi fami
title: Belonging by Sonia Gandhi review – India’s elder stateswoman breaks her silence

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
The wait for the new Bond is over but that’s only the beginning – there are still small issues such as the script, title, setting, casting, branding and promotion …

• Robert Pattinson announced as James Bond – news
• Share your thoughts on the casting
• Peter Bradshaw’s take
• Pattinson’s journey to James Bond
• Behind Bond’s bankability

It’s official:
title: Robert Pattinson is James Bond. So what happens next?

author: Peter Bradshaw
description:
Teodora Ana Mihai and her passionately committed cast reconstruct the grim sequence of bad judgments that led to 39 fans dying

Shame and rage are the keynotes of this immersive, viscerally powerful drama-thriller set amid the macabre tragedy of football’s 1985 European Cup final between Juventus and Liverpool in the crumbling Heysel stadium in Brussels. Crowd disorder before kickoff in a poorly maintained, badly policed venue resulted in the deaths of 39 fans. In this film, the roar of the crowd echoing overhead through the stadium’s claustrophobic tunnels is like the wailing of the damned, while the sport’s officer class flinch and panic as if at a wartime loss. Grimly, the match was allowed to go ahead, despite the fatalities; the authorities believed the game itself would restore order on a bread-and-circuses basis, and that abandoning the match would only cause greater
title: Heysel 85 review – rage-filled denunciation of the incompetence that fuelled a football disaster

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Influenced by jazz, Cuban photographer Julio Mitchel has spent his career documenting the problems that plague countries from Venezuela to Peru

Continue reading...
title: ‘I confront my demons’: crime, corruption and poverty in Latin America – in pictures

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
New tech wealth, amassed with remarkable speed, is now washing up on British shores

Sporting hoodies and white trainers rather than the gilets of London’s banker and lawyer class, tech bros can struggle to be taken seriously by the capital’s luxury property agents. “We worked with a young tech entrepreneur with a substantial budget, who agents assumed was looking to rent a one-bedroom flat,” says Jo Eccles, a buying agent who sources off-market properties for ultra-wealthy clients.

But this week’s float by Anthropic, the AI developer behind the chatbot Claude, promises to bring even more credibility for the growing cohort of tech millionaires, which could breathe life into London’s ailing high-end property market. Its IPO on Thursday, expected to value the company at $1.4tn (£1.1m), is likely to turn more than 4,000 of its staff into millionaires as their stock o
title: Millionaire factory: Anthropic IPO set to fuel AI gold rush in London’s high-end property market

author: Sarah Crown
description:
Fifteen years on, this expansive follow-up to the campus epic explores female agency, friendship – and the messiness of early adulthood

Back in 2011, Chad Harbach’s debut The Art of Fielding was hailed as the next Great American Novel. Set on the campus of Westish, a fictional midwestern liberal arts college, and steeped in baseball, it grappled with the big, quintessentially American themes – ambition, failure, the pursuit of perfection – that have traditionally been the genre’s hallmark. Harbach himself winkingly invited the categorisation: The Art of Fielding communes directly with the spirit of Herman Melville, arguably the greatest Great American Novelist of them all. Westish College, the novel explains, has claimed Melville as its own since the discovery of a lecture he gave there in 1880: its baseball team is known as the Harpooners; and a Melville statue presides ove
title: The Brightness by Chad Harbach review – an ambitious sequel to The Art of Fielding

author: Catherine Shoard
description:
An infestation at my hotel meant my clothes had to be fumigated. When I turned up in shorts to interview the actor, he lent me his jacket, but I suspect he may have regretted it

The biting flies were wild in Toronto in September 2012. A colleague and I were there to cover the film festival, but our key reference that year was a zinger from the 2007 cartoon Bee Movie, when it turns out Chris Rock’s mosquito has become a lawyer: “I was already a bloodsucking parasite,” he says, “all I needed was a briefcase!” (Bee Movie is one of the most brilliant and adult children’s movies ever; its central premise compares the honey industry to concentration camps.)

Anyway, I spent the first week getting ever more bloodless and lumpy. We even shot a video about them, spraying repellent in front of us like Mace. It didn’t w
title: The pest I’ll never forget: the bedbugs that bit me – and worried Jake Gyllenhaal

author: Sami Tamimi
description:
Falling-apart-tender lamb with jewelled, nutty bulgur wheat is a riot of texture and flavour

These dishes were made to sit together. The lamb is slowly cooked with quince and saffron, bringing richness, warmth and a gentle sweetness, while the maftoul offers a lighter contrast with its lemon, currants and toasted almonds, and provides the perfect base for the fragrant meat juices. It’s a generous combination; simple enough for a family meal, but special enough to share with friends.

Continue reading...
title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for lamb and quince tagine with maftoul

author: Gaby Hinsliff
description:
The law is important, but so is the fact that people know when associates embark on inappropriate relationships. They bear responsibility too

Mia Latter was 16 and out clothes-shopping when Russell Brand stopped her on the street. He riffled through her bags to choose a dress he told her she should wear for the date he’d be taking her on. And so began a short relationship – if that’s the right word, given she was still at school and he was a 30-year-old MTV presenter, who she says publicly referred to her as “the child”. Towards the end, she claims, Brand orally raped her.

Lilly Creightmore was 18 when she says the then 32-year-old celebrity David Walliams
title: Don’t wait for a change in the age of consent. Adults can act to stop age-gap abuse | Gaby Hinsliff

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye

Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.

About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

Continue reading...
title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

author: Exclusive by Paul MacInnes
description:
• Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges

  • Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body

The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action.

Fifa is a signatory to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”.
title: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion

author: Susan Chenery
description:
Inquest continues into deaths of four babies born in free births or home births in northern rivers

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A northern rivers mother whose baby died after a free birth did not know she was having twins until she was in labour after having no pregnancy scans, the New South Wales coroner’s court has heard.

The inquest will examine the deaths of four babies born in free births or home births who died in the northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024. It will consider whether the care was reasonable in the circumstances and whether care by an unregistered support worker was reasonable and appropriate before, during and after the birth. Free births are when a person gives birth without a register
title: Woman whose baby died after free birth didn’t know she was pregnant with twins, NSW inquest hears

author: Mark Rosenblatt
description:
The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol by Complicité conjured the struggles of a French village with an intense rawness

There are many things you see that are impactful, but few you can genuinely say change your life. I saw Complicité’s The Three Lives of Lucie Cabrol aged 16 on a school trip to Riverside Studios in London and it really reached me. I’d been educated in a very language, words-based way. Here the story was told – with such intensity! – through people’s bodies.

The world they were conjuring, from a story by John Berger in his book Pig Earth, was about this remote French village – a world of labour. And the strife and struggles of these characters was expressed through the physical work of the company.

Giant can be seen in cinemas from 19 November

As told to Lindesay Irvine
title: The play that changed my life: ‘John Berger’s Pig Earth became something magical – they licked milk off bodies’

author: Rachel Dixon
description:
If you discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds when consuming fruit and vegetables you are missing out on a lot of value. Here’s what to incorporate into your diet – and what to avoid

Do you peel your potatoes, deseed your squash and core your cauliflower? A study by King’s College London, published last month in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, found that people who routinely discard peels, skins, stalks and seeds when preparing fruit and vegetables are missing out on a valuable source of dietary fibre. Ten out of the 12 types of produce the researchers analysed had higher levels of fibre in the scraps than in the flesh. Eating these often overlooked parts could help address the global dietary fibre deficit and tackle food waste, they say. Here, experts share their advi
title: The root-to-tip revolution! An A-Z of how to eat plants in full – for extra flavour, fibre and savings

author: Ruth Michaelson
description:
Mada Masr, the news site co-founded by Lina Attalah just before the 2013 military coup, is fighting for its life after being shut down, but its journalists have not given up hope

Facing a year in prison for running Egypt’s leading independent news outlet Mada Masr, Lina Attalah is trying to focus on the everyday: waking at dawn to hear the birds sing before Cairo’s streets come alive and visiting Mada Masr’s shuttered offices with her reporters to water the plants and feed their four cats.

Attalah is the reluctant face of Egypt’s embattled independent press at a moment of crisis. In the last six weeks, Egyptian authorities have waged a renewed crackdown on the few remaining independent media outlets left in the country, beginning with the arrest of the entire newsroom of
title: ‘I’m not ready to go to jail’: co-founder of Egypt’s last independent media outlet faces prison

author: Fiona Harvey and Simon Evans in Antalya
description:
Analysis of fossil fuel exports since 1850 differs from most assessments – which look at countries where CO2 is released

Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are the three biggest exporters of carbon dioxide in history, according to analysis of fossil fuels since 1850.

Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Accounting for the CO2 produced by burning these exports, Russia has been responsible for more than 70 gigatonnes, up to the end of 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia named as biggest CO2 exporters in history

author: Guy de Launey in Belgrade
description:
Inaugural parliamentary session comes as ousted populist Aleksandar Vučić threatens mass protests of his own

Candidates for Serbia’s Student List, the grassroots movement of political outsiders that pulled off a spectacular victory in last month’s elections over the party of the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić, are to be sworn in as MPs as they begin the process of forming a government.

The 140 candidates – among them academics, lawyers, scientists and the odd actor – will be sworn in on Tuesday during the inaugural session of the new parliament, bringing 14 years of rule by Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) to an end.

title: Serbia’s Student List candidates to be sworn in as MPs after election triumph

author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Keza MacDonald; produced by Tom Glasser, Guy Szafman and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent
description:
This week, after a 13-year wait, gamers will finally get hold of Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest instalment of the most successful console computer game in history.

There have been $1bn worth of pre-orders already, says the Guardian’s video games editor, Keza MacDonald.

How did a game of stealing cars and shooting strangers become such an enormous cultural phenomenon? Keza traces the history of games by Rockstar, GTA’s creator, and what its most successful product has told us about the US, the setting of all its games so far.

And what, asks Annie Kelly, can fans expect when they start playing GTA VI?

Read more:

Ten years, thousands of staff and a billion dollars: the exclusive inside story of Grand Theft Auto VI
title: Grand Theft Auto VI: the cultural event of the decade? - podcast

author: Ben Doherty
description:
Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’

Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.

Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.

Continue reading...
title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine

description:
Knit hat caught in ceiling fan and flung into enclosure eaten by Fiona, who is being closely monitored by zoo staff

The Cincinnati zoo says Fiona, its beloved hippo who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat that got into her enclosure.

Zoo veterinarians and staff are monitoring Fiona and working to help her pass the hat, the zoo said in a statement Monday.
